proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress wind down the Title VI international and area studies programs at universities, which it says sometimes fund programs counter to American interests. In the meantime it recommends a new regulation requiring the Secretary to allocate at least 40 percent of funding to international business programs that teach free markets and economics, and to require institutions, faculty and fellowship recipients to certify that they intend to serve American interests.
remaining: Congressional repeal or phase-out of Title VI, which the FY2026 law did not do.

A regulation allocating at least 40 percent to international business programs and requiring certifications of service to American interests; the 2026-07-01 proposal would remove program regulations and contains neither.

status_summary: Executive action has curtailed Fulbright-Hays grants and proposed removing the Title VI and Fulbright-Hays program regulations, while the programs remain in statute. On 2025-05-09 ED cancelled the FY2025 competitions for three Fulbright-Hays programs (90 FR 19688). On 2025-11-18 ED announced a partnership moving Fulbright-Hays administration to the State Department, which trade press reported also covers the Title VI programs, and on 2026-07-01 ED proposed rescinding all of its Title VI and Fulbright-Hays program regulations (91 FR 39945), stating that the programs would remain governed by statute; comments closed 2026-07-31 and no final rule was found. The consolidated FY2026 appropriations act (H.R. 7148) was signed 2026-02-03, and the Title VI and Fulbright-Hays amounts in it were not confirmed from the act or an agency document; no statute winding down Title VI and no rule setting a 40 percent international business share or certification requirement was found.

timeline.event: ED withdrew the FY2025 notices inviting applications and cancelled the competitions for the Fulbright-Hays Group Projects Abroad, Doctoral Dissertation Research Abroad and Faculty Research Abroad programs (90 FR 19688), citing a review to align priorities with administration goals.

ED announced an International Education and Foreign Language Studies Partnership with the State Department covering programs administered under Fulbright-Hays (the ED page shows a last-reviewed date of 2025-11-18).

The President signed H.R. 7148, the FY2026 consolidated appropriations act; CRS reports that its Division B carries the full-year Labor, HHS and Education appropriations (P.L. 119-75). The Title VI and Fulbright-Hays amounts in the act were not confirmed.
The FY2027 budget request proposed eliminating the Title VI International Education program, described as currently funded at $81 million, per a university federal relations summary.

ED published a proposed rule to rescind its regulations for the Title VI international education programs and the Fulbright-Hays programs (34 CFR parts 655 to 664 and 669; 91 FR 39945), stating the programs would remain governed by statute; comments closed 2026-07-31.

title: Wind down HEA Title VI area studies; interim 40 percent business share and certifications
uncertainties: A higher-education association summary dated by its URL to 2025-09-19 reports that ED ended Title VI international education grants through non-continuation notices as inconsistent with administration priorities and moved about $86 million of FY2025 funds to HBCUs; no ED notice or news report confirming this was found, so it is unverified and is not counted. Separately, the FY2026 amounts were not confirmed in the appropriations law text, which could not be read past its first division. The FY2026 amounts of $70.4 million for Title VI and $10.3 million for Fulbright-Hays come from an association summary that was not opened in this check and remain unverified; a CRS report on FY2026 Labor, HHS and Education appropriations was opened but its readable text has no Department of Education program lines. The White House signing page names the act the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, while CRS calls it the Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75). The ED release on the State partnership names only Fulbright-Hays; the inclusion of Title VI programs and the count of 12 programs come from The PIE News. The PIE News and an association summary say the House FY2026 bill provided nothing for Title VI. The $81 million in the FY2027 summary may be the combined Title VI and Fulbright-Hays line, which is an inference not confirmed from a primary document. The 2025-05-09 notice cancelled three Fulbright-Hays competitions (Group Projects Abroad, Doctoral Dissertation Research Abroad and Faculty Research Abroad) rather than every Fulbright-Hays program. Whether ED or State has run new Title VI competitions with FY2026 funds was not found. The closure of the International and Foreign Language Education office was not confirmed. The University of Michigan reported that its Title VI centers operated until 2025-09-10 and listed its programs as canceled; that page is context only.
